title: Ponzo Illusion
content: The Ponzo Illusion demonstrates the principle that our minds estimate the size of an object based on surrounding background cues.The illusion was first described by Italian psychologist Mario Ponzo in 1913. In its simplest form, the illustration showstwo lines of equal length are placed at an angle between two diagonal lines.The line placed on the top appears to be longer than the one on the bottom. This is because the brain interprets the diagonal lines as converging in perspective, and therefore the upper line must be longer. But of course the segments are really exactly the same size.The illusion is more compelling when the background cues are more realistic. In this case, all three cars are exactly the same size.More examplesWikipedia on Ponzo Illusion
